subject: Quick quote for Aurora case study — hold pending incident review
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Martinez <olivia@auroraanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick quote for Aurora case study

Hi Olivia,

Thanks again for the conversation this week — the Aurora team has been a great partner and the results you shared are compelling. We are putting together a short case study to highlight the latency and cost improvements you realized after moving certain inference paths onto Redwood Dedicated. Would you be open to a 1–2 sentence quote we can use in the case study and on our site? A couple of options are fine.

If helpful, I attached a one-page brief that explains the format. No legal redlines required for a short customer quote, but if you want us to run it by your team we can. Ideally we’d have something by July 20 so marketing can hit our July cadence.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0147

Attachments: case_study_brief.pdf (stub)

Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick quote for Aurora case study

Hi Ben,

Thanks — happy to help. Here’s a short quote you can use: "Redwood’s serving runtime cut our average 95th-percentile latency by over 40% and let our team scale predictions without blowing up costs."

I attached a 1-page doc with the quote and a preferred attribution line (Olivia Martinez, Head of Data, Aurora Analytics). If you need anything edited for length, let me know — otherwise this is good to publish once we have sign-off.

Best,
Olivia

Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Quick quote for Aurora case study — incident note

Hi team,

Heads up — Aurora reported a production incident on July 13 (brief outage affecting some prediction pipelines). Their CS contact said the impact was limited and resolved, but churn signals are slightly elevated (they have a renewal conversation in Q4). I pulled a short incident summary from our CS notes and attached it.

Given the timing and the fact that this quote calls out performance improvements, I recommend we pause publication of the quote until we confirm there are no lingering concerns on Aurora's side and until legal/marketing have reviewed the messaging.

Can we get a quick leadership sign-off to hold the quote? If approved, I’ll reach out to Olivia to request permission to temporarily hold the quote and explain it’s due to timing — she should be looped in on the next steps.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: incident_summary.pdf (stub)

Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick quote for Aurora case study — incident note

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the heads up and the summary.

Agreed: please pause any publication activity. Ben, hold the quote from marketing and do not post or push to the website until we have confirmation from Aurora and a final legal/marketing check.

Marketing/legal: can you weigh in with any messaging concerns? If marketing wants to rephrase to avoid specific numbers, we should propose alternate language to Aurora.

Marissa, please draft the outreach to Olivia and include the incident summary and optional rewording suggestions for marketing to review. Vivek — if you’re OK with a temporary hold I’ll mark this as approved pending the outreach result.

-Stephanie

Hi Olivia,

I wanted to follow up on the quote you kindly provided last week. We’ve had an internal review after Aurora’s incident on July 13 and, out of an abundance of caution, we’d like to temporarily pause publication of the case study and any public attribution until we confirm there are no outstanding concerns on your side.

Would you be comfortable if we hold the quote for now? We aren’t looking to remove it permanently — just to delay publication until you confirm things are stable and your team is comfortable. If you prefer, we can share a short statement that avoids specific percent improvements while still acknowledging the partnership.

For reference, I’m including your original note below.
